questions.question: As per the NITI Aayog Report titled 'FAST TRACKING FREIGHT IN INDIA' of 2021, what was the share of road transport in the freight traffic?

• According to the NITI Aayog report titled **'FAST TRACKING FREIGHT IN INDIA' (2021)**, the road transport sector accounted for **71% of the freight traffic in India**.

questions.question: The present cost of a hospital is ₹1,82,590. After a year, its cost increased to ₹1,95,382. The percentage increase (rounded off to the nearest integer) in the cost of the hospital is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Cost increase = 1,95,382 − 1,82,590 = 12,792

Percentage increase = (12,792 ÷ 1,82,590) × 100

Approximate 1% of 1,82,590 ≈ 1,826. Since 1,826 × 7 = 12,782, the value is ≈ 7%.

**∴ The correct answer is 7%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Original Cost = ₹1,82,590

New Cost = ₹1,95,382

**Formula Used:**

Percentage Increase = [(New Value − Original Value) ÷ Original Value] × 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4790c0fdd9d710d2af7ff4497c4bd2552a7e625c2636b37e834b8f724877c879.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Total Increase = 1,95,382 − 1,82,590 = 12,792

⇒ Percentage Increase = (12,792 ÷ 1,82,590) × 100

⇒ Percentage Increase ≈ 0.070058 × 100

⇒ Percentage Increase ≈ 7.0058%

⇒ Rounded to nearest integer = 7%

**∴ The correct answer is 7%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Percentage Change

It represents the relationship between an old value and a new value. Formula: [(Difference) ÷ (Original Value)] × 100.

Rounding Off Rules

If the decimal part is 0.5 or more, round up to the next integer; otherwise, keep the current integer.

Base Value in Percentage

Always use the initial or original value as the denominator (base) when calculating the percentage of increase or decrease.

• **Role of the Council of Ministers:**
 
 
• The Council of Ministers, headed by the Prime Minister, assists the President in drafting the speech.
 
• This ensures that the address reflects the collective policy decisions and priorities of the government.
 
 
 
• **Importance of the Presidential Address:**
 
 
• It sets the tone for parliamentary discussions and debates for the upcoming session.

• **Arya Samaj:**
 
 
• Founded by Dayanand Saraswati in 1875, Arya Samaj emphasized the Vedas as the ultimate source of knowledge and guidance.
 
• It advocated social reforms such as the abolition of caste discrimination, child marriage, and untouchability.
 
 
 
• **Bahujan Samaj:**

• He authored several important works, including "Gulamgiri" (Slavery), which critiqued the caste system and called for equality.

questions.question: The percentage profit earned by selling a table lamp for ₹214 is equal to the percentage loss incurred by selling the same table lamp for ₹146. At what price (in ₹) should the table lamp be sold to make 55% profit?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When **Profit% = Loss%** for two different selling prices, the **Cost Price (CP)** is the average of the two prices.

CP = (214 + 146) ÷ 2 = 360 ÷ 2 = ₹180.

To make **55% profit**, required SP = CP × (100 + P%) ÷ 100.

Required SP = 180 × 155 ÷ 100 = 1.8 × 155 = ₹279.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹279.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** SP₁ = ₹214, SP₂ = ₹146, Profit% at SP₁ = Loss% at SP₂, New Profit% = 55%.

**Formulas:** Profit = SP − CP | Loss = CP − SP | SP = CP × (1 + P/100).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/92bfc01e0b5cc08908451501e1ac129571e28d13520dc29933418add639fb42b.png] 

⇒ Let the CP be x. Since Profit% = Loss%, (214 − x)/x × 100 = (x − 146)/x × 100.

⇒ 214 − x = x − 146 ⇒ 2x = 360 ⇒ x = 180.

⇒ New Selling Price = 180 × (100 + 55) ÷ 100 = 180 × 1.55.

⇒ New Selling Price = 180 × 155 / 100 = 27900 / 100 = ₹279.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹279.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Symmetric Profit and Loss

When numerical profit equals numerical loss for two different prices, CP is the mid-point. If **Profit% = Loss%**, CP is still the arithmetic mean of the two SPs.

Percentage Calculations

To calculate a value after x% increase: **New Value = Original Value × (1 + x/100)**.

questions.question: At what rate (in percentage) per annum will ₹1,300 give ₹650 as simple interest in 10 years?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

**Simple Interest (SI)** per year = 650 ÷ 10 = ₹65

**Rate** % = (Interest for 1 year ÷ Principal) × 100

**Rate** = (65 ÷ 1300) × 100

**Rate** = 5%

**∴ The correct answer is 5%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Principal (P)** = ₹1,300

**Simple Interest (SI)** = ₹650

**Time (T)** = 10 years

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7e26d5e13d8bee6a03b57e6905cc07e94fabf06512a79b1a5de4821d1964ec66.png] 

**Formula Used:**

SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

**Calculations:**

⇒ 650 = (1300 × R × 10) ÷ 100

⇒ 650 = (13000 × R) ÷ 100

⇒ 650 = 130 × R

⇒ R = 650 ÷ 130

⇒ R = 5%

**∴ The correct answer is 5%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Simple Interest Concept

Interest is calculated only on the **original principal** amount throughout the entire period. SI = P × R × T / 100.

Total Amount Formula

The final sum of money is called the **Amount**. Amount (A) = Principal (P) + Simple Interest (SI).

Finding Time or Principal

Using the same base formula, **Time (T)** = (SI × 100) ÷ (P × R) and **Principal (P)** = (SI × 100) ÷ (R × T).

questions.question: If 5x + 4y = 12 and xy = 2, then find the value of 125x³ + 64y³.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Use the algebraic identity: **(a + b)³ = a³ + b³ + 3ab(a + b)**.

Here, let a = **5x** and b = **4y**, then a + b = **12** and ab = 5 × 4 × xy = 20 × 2 = **40**.

Applying the formula: 125x³ + 64y³ = (5x + 4y)³ − 3(5x)(4y)(5x + 4y).

Result = 12³ − 3 × 40 × 12 = 1728 − 1440 = 288.

**∴ The correct answer is 288.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** 5x + 4y = 12 and xy = 2.

**Formula Used:** (a + b)³ = a³ + b³ + 3ab(a + b)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/645cda575df26ce2f9e668ddb58e429195abdc7ce427130ec2b0ab1936c96c69.png] 

To find the value of **125x³ + 64y³**, we cube both sides of the given equation **5x + 4y = 12**:

⇒ (5x + 4y)³ = (12)³

⇒ (5x)³ + (4y)³ + 3 × (5x) × (4y) × (5x + 4y) = 1728

⇒ 125x³ + 64y³ + 3 × (20xy) × (12) = 1728

⇒ 125x³ + 64y³ + 36 × 20 × (2) = 1728

⇒ 125x³ + 64y³ + 1440 = 1728

⇒ 125x³ + 64y³ = 1728 − 1440

⇒ 125x³ + 64y³ = 288

**∴ The correct answer is 288.**

**__Additional Information__**

Cubic Sum Identity

(a + b)³ = a³ + b³ + 3ab(a + b). It can also be written as a³ + b³ = (a + b)³ − 3ab(a + b).

Cubic Difference Identity

(a − b)³ = a³ − b³ − 3ab(a − b). This is useful for finding the difference of cubes when the product and difference are known.

Factorization of Cubes

a³ + b³ = (a + b)(a² − ab + b²) and a³ − b³ = (a − b)(a² + ab + b²).</p

Divisibility Rule of 7 (Osculator Method)

Subtract twice the last digit from the rest of the number. If the result is 0 or a multiple of 7, the original number is divisible by 7.

The difference between the sum of digits at **odd places** and the sum of digits at **even places** must be 0 or a multiple of 11.

questions.question: Two quadratic equations, x² - 5x + 6 = 0 and 2x² - kx + 6 = 0, have one common root. What is the possible value of k?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Solve the first **quadratic equation**: x² − 5x + 6 = 0 ⇒ (x − 2)(x − 3) = 0. Roots are **2** and **3**.

Substitute **x = 2** in the second equation: 2(2)² − k(2) + 6 = 0 ⇒ 8 − 2k + 6 = 0 ⇒ 2k = 14 ⇒ **k = 7**.

Substitute **x = 3** in the second equation: 2(3)² − k(3) + 6 = 0 ⇒ 18 − 3k + 6 = 0 ⇒ 3k = 24 ⇒ **k = 8**.

Comparing the values with the given options, the valid **possible value of k** is 7.

**∴ The correct answer is 7.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Equations x² − 5x + 6 = 0 and 2x² − kx + 6 = 0 share a **common root**.

**Step 1:** Find the roots of the first equation.

⇒ x² − 5x + 6 = 0

⇒ x² − 3x − 2x + 6 = 0

⇒ x(x − 3) − 2(x − 3) = 0

⇒ (x − 3)(x − 2) = 0

⇒ **x = 2** or **x = 3**

**Step 2:** Substitute these roots into the second equation to find **k**.

If **x = 2** is the common root:

⇒ 2(2)² − k(2) + 6 = 0

⇒ 2(4) − 2k + 6 = 0

⇒ 8 − 2k + 6 = 0

⇒ 14 − 2k = 0

questions.question: A pouch contains 50 Paise, 25 Paise, and 10 Paise coins in the ratio 18 : 12 : 10, amounting to ₹130. Find the number of 10 Paise coins.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Convert all values to **Paise** units for easier calculation.

Value ratio = (18 × 50) : (12 × 25) : (10 × 10) = 900 : 300 : 100 = 9 : 3 : 1.

Total units = 9 + 3 + 1 = 13 units → ₹130 (or 13000 Paise).

1 unit = ₹10. Since 10 Paise coins make up 1 unit of the total value, their value is ₹10 (1000 Paise).

Number of 10 Paise coins = 1000 ÷ 10 = 100 coins.

**∴ The correct answer is 100 coins.**

⇒ Value of 25P coins = 12x × 0.25 = ₹3x

⇒ Value of 10P coins = 10x × 0.10 = ₹1x

⇒ Total Amount: 9x + 3x + 1x = 130

⇒ 13x = 130

⇒ x = 10

⇒ Number of 10 Paise coins = 10x = 10 × 10 = 100

**∴ The correct answer is 100 coins.**

**__Additional Information__**

Ratio of Value vs Ratio of Number

questions.question: A and B complete a work in 20 days. If A alone can do it in 45 days, then B alone can do one-third of the same work in _______ days.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Work rate of **B** = (1/20) − (1/45) = (9 − 4) / 180 = 5 / 180 = 1 / 36.

Total time for **B** alone = 36 days.

Time for 1/3 of the work = 36 × (1/3) = 12 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 12 days.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Time taken by **A + B** = 20 days

Time taken by **A** alone = 45 days

**Formula Used:**

Efficiency = Total Work ÷ Time

 
 **Person** **Days** **Total Work** **Efficiency** 
 **A + B** 20 180 9 
 **A** 45 4 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Efficiency of **B** = Efficiency of (A + B) − Efficiency of A

⇒ Efficiency of **B** = 9 − 4 = 5 units/day

⇒ Total work to be done by **B** = 1/3 × 180 = 60 units

⇒ Time taken by **B** = 60 ÷ 5 = 12 days

**∴ The correct answer is 12 days.**

**__Additional Information__**

Pipes & Cisterns Relation

The concept of Time and Work is identical to filling a tank. If two pipes fill a tank in T days and one fills in T₁, the other takes (T × T₁) ÷ (T₁ − T) days.

Work & Wages

Wages are distributed in the direct **ratio of the efficiency** of the workers or the ratio of work done.

Alternate Day Work

In alternate day problems, calculate work done in a **2-day cycle** first, then multiply to reach near the total work.</p

questions.question: The average of 10 observations is 40. It was realised later that an observation was misread as 31 in place of 50. Find the correct average.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Net difference in observations = **Correct value** − **Incorrect value** = 50 − 31 = +19.

Adjustment in average = Net difference ÷ **Total observations** = 19 ÷ 10 = +1.9.

Correct average = **Old Average** + Adjustment = 40 + 1.9 = 41.9.

**∴ The correct answer is 41.9.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Number of observations (n) = 10

Initial **Average** = 40

**Incorrect observation** = 31

**Correct observation** = 50

**Formula Used:**

Average = Sum of observations ÷ Number of observations

Correct Sum = (Initial Average × n) − Incorrect Value + Correct Value

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36696c1646c6422d04192d7ce4c81b8f422c0796d714552e3d3994f94a5e6b09.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Initial Sum = 40 × 10 = 400

⇒ Correct Sum = 400 − 31 + 50

⇒ Correct Sum = 369 + 50 = 419

⇒ Correct Average = 419 ÷ 10

⇒ Correct Average = 41.9

**∴ The correct answer is 41.9.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Effect of Change on Average

If each observation is increased or decreased by a constant 'k', the average also increases or decreases by 'k'. New Average = Old Average ± k.

Weighted Average

When two groups with averages A₁ and A₂ and sizes n₁ and n₂ are combined, the combined average is (n₁A₁ + n₂A₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).

Net Deviation Method

The sum of deviations of all observations from their mean is always zero. This property is used to quickly find missing values or corrections.</p

questions.question: If 48, 96, 20 and y are in proportion, then the value of y is:
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

For **four numbers** a, b, c, d to be in **proportion**, the product of extremes equals the product of means (ad = bc).

Given: 48, 96, 20, y are in **proportion**.

Ratio of first two = 48 : 96 = 1 : 2.

Ratio of next two must be same ⇒ 20 : y = 1 : 2.

∴ y = 20 × 2 = 40.

**∴ The correct answer is 40.**

⇒ 1/2 = 20/y

⇒ y = 20 × 2

⇒ y = 40

**∴ The correct answer is 40.**

**__Additional Information__**

Fourth Proportional

The **fourth proportional** to three numbers a, b, and c is d such that a : b = c : d, calculated as d = (b × c) / a.

Continued Proportion

Three numbers a, b, and c are in **continued proportion** if a : b = b : c, where b is the **mean proportional** (b = √ac).

Componendo and Dividendo

If a/b = c/d, then (a + b)/(a − b) = (c + d)/(c − d). This rule is widely used to solve **ratio-based equations** quickly.</p

questions.question: The average of fifty numbers is 34. If two numbers, namely 34 and 22 are discarded, the average of the remaining numbers is:
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Discarding **34** (which is the **original average**) doesn't change the average of the remaining 49 numbers.

Discarding **22**, which is (34 − 22) = **12** less than the average, creates a **surplus**.

This surplus is distributed over the remaining (50 − 2) = **48** numbers.

Increase in **Average** = 12 ÷ 48 = **0.25**.

New **Average** = 34 + 0.25 = **34.25**.

**∴ The correct answer is 34.25.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** The average of **50 numbers** is **34**. Two numbers, **34** and **22**, are discarded.

**Formula Used:** Average = Sum of all observations ÷ Total number of observations

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/28aedbc3e3f9288b686f7abe6049a74b537bbcbc6430879772b12c29c42e7ba1.png] 

⇒ **Initial Total Sum** = Average × Count = 34 × 50 = **1700**

⇒ Sum of discarded numbers = 34 + 22 = **56**

⇒ **New Sum** after discarding = 1700 − 56 = **1644**

⇒ **New Count** of numbers = 50 − 2 = **48**

⇒ **New Average** = New Sum ÷ New Count = 1644 ÷ 48

⇒ New Average = **34.25**

**∴ The correct answer is 34.25.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Property of Average when removing values

If the discarded number is **greater** than the average, the new average **decreases**. If the discarded number is **smaller** than the average, the new average **increases**.

Uniform Change

If every number in a set is increased or decreased by a constant **k**, the **average** also increases or decreases by **k** respectively.

Weighted Average

When two groups with averages A₁ and A₂ and counts n₁ and n₂ are combined, the combined average is (n₁A₁ + n₂A₂) ÷ (n₁ + n₂).</p

questions.question: In finding the HCF of two numbers by division method, the quotients are 1, 5, and 8, respectively, and the last divisor is 57. What is the LCM of the two numbers?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Work backward from the last divisor: **HCF** = 57.

Divisor₃ = 57 × 8 = 456 (Second number)

Divisor₂ = 456 × 5 + 57 = 2337 (First number)

Divisor₁ = 2337 × 1 + 456 = 2793

**LCM** = (2337 × 2793) ÷ 57 = 114513.

**∴ The correct answer is 114513.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/439aad8a4efc95561159fb2d3cc2d29cd1a763176aae61bc1b6e01a1083f3aa3.png] 

**Given:** Quotients = 1, 5, 8; Last divisor (HCF) = 57.

**Formula Used:** Dividend = (Divisor × Quotient) + Remainder

⇒ **Third Dividend** = (57 × 8) + 0 = 456

⇒ **Second Dividend** = (456 × 5) + 57 = 2280 + 57 = 2337

⇒ **First Dividend** = (2337 × 1) + 456 = 2793

⇒ Two numbers are 2337 and 2793.

⇒ **LCM** = (Product of numbers) ÷ HCF

⇒ **LCM** = (2337 × 2793) ÷ 57

⇒ **LCM** = 41 × 2793 = 114513

**∴ The correct answer is 114513.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

HCF by Long Division

This method involves **successive division** where the remainder of one step becomes the divisor for the next step until the remainder is zero.

Relation between HCF and LCM

For any two numbers a and b: **a × b = HCF(a, b) × LCM(a, b)**. This is used to find one value when the other three are known.

Properties of HCF

The **HCF** of two or more numbers is the greatest number that divides each of them exactly without leaving a remainder.</p

questions.question: Which type of muscle fibres are primarily found in the gastrointestinal tract, and what is a key characteristic of their contraction?

options.text: Skeletal muscle fibres, rapid and voluntary contraction
Cardiac muscle fibres, rhythmic and involuntary contraction
Striated muscle fibres, intermittent and forceful contraction
Smooth muscle fibres, slow and sustained involuntary contraction

questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 4,Key Points

 
• Muscle fibres in the gastrointestinal tract are primarily **smooth muscle fibres**, which are essential for its function.
 
• **Smooth muscle fibres** are responsible for slow, sustained, and involuntary contractions that facilitate processes like peristalsis.
 
• These fibres are **non-striated**, meaning they lack the organized sarcomere structure seen in skeletal and cardiac muscles.
 
• Smooth muscle contractions are regulated by the **autonomic nervous system**, making them involuntary.
 
• They play a crucial role in the movement of food, absorption, and digestion within the gastrointestinal tract.

Additional Information

 
• **Skeletal Muscle Fibres**

 
 
• Skeletal muscles are striated and under voluntary control.
 
• They are responsible for movement and posture through rapid and forceful contractions.
 
• They are attached to bones via tendons.
 
 
 
• **Cardiac Muscle Fibres**
 
 
• Cardiac muscles are striated and involuntary.
 
• They are exclusively found in the heart and are responsible for rhythmic contractions.
 
• Contractions are regulated by pacemaker cells and the autonomic nervous system.
 
 
 
• **Peristalsis**
 
 
• A wave-like motion produced by smooth muscle contractions in the gastrointestinal tract.
 
• It helps in propelling food and digestive contents forward.
 
 
 
• **Autonomic Nervous System (ANS)**
 
 
• ANS controls involuntary functions in the body, including smooth muscle activity.
 
• The ANS consists of the sympathetic and parasympathetic divisions.

questions.question: The curved surface area of a right circular cone is 2684π cm², and the diameter of its base is 44 cm. Find the height (in cm) of the cone.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Given **Diameter** = 44 cm → **Radius (r)** = 22 cm.

**Curved Surface Area (CSA)** = πrl = 2684π ⇒ 22 × l = 2684.

**Slant height (l)** = 2684 ÷ 22 = 122 cm.

Apply **Pythagoras Theorem**: h = √(l² − r²) = √(122² − 22²) = √((122 − 22)(122 + 22)).

h = √(100 × 144) = 10 × 12 = 120 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 120 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

**Curved Surface Area (CSA)** = 2684π cm²

**Diameter** = 44 cm ⇒ **Radius (r)** = 44 ÷ 2 = 22 cm

**Formula Used:**

Curved Surface Area of cone = πrl

Slant height (l) = √(h² + r²)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/799d616b3777c61d296d271fa3050187dd9687cb04e70b4baf29508bedf8aa59.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ π × 22 × l = 2684π

⇒ 22 × l = 2684

⇒ l = 2684 ÷ 22 = 122 cm

⇒ l² = r² + h²

⇒ 122² = 22² + h²

⇒ h² = 122² − 22²

⇒ h² = (122 − 22)(122 + 22) [Using a² − b² = (a−b)(a+b)]

⇒ h² = 100 × 144

⇒ h = √(14400) = 120 cm

**∴ The correct answer is 120 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Total Surface Area of Cone

It includes the curved area and the circular base area: TSA = πr(l + r).

Volume of Cone

The space occupied by the cone: V = (1/3)πr²h.

Slant Height Relation

In a right circular cone, the height, radius, and slant height form a right-angled triangle: l² = h² + r².</p

questions.question: "Purvang" and "Uttarang" are two sections of which of the components of Carnatic Music?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Varnam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Purvang** and **Uttarang** are two integral sections of a Varnam__, a fundamental compositional form in Carnatic music.
 
• The **Purvang** (first section) typically consists of the __Pallavi, Anupallavi, and Muktayi Swaras__, while the **Uttarang** (second section) includes the __Charanam and Charana Swaras__.
 
• Varnam serves as an introductory piece in Carnatic music concerts and is used for both __performance and practice__.
 
• It is designed to showcase the raga's essence through a combination of **melodic and rhythmic elements**.
 
• Varnams are critical for improving a musician's mastery of **raga alapana, swara singing, and rhythm**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Varnam in Carnatic Music**

 
 
• It is an important compositional form in Carnatic music with both lyrical and swara-based__ segments.
 
• There are two types of Varnams: **Tana Varnam** (focused on swaras) and **Pada Varnam** (focused on lyrical content).
 
• It serves as a warm-up for vocalists and instrumentalists due to its complexity and extensive range of notes.
 
 
 
• **Pallavi, Anupallavi, and Charanam**
 __
 
• **Pallavi:** The main thematic line of the composition, repeated throughout.
 
• **Anupallavi:** A short stanza that complements the Pallavi, often elaborating on its theme.
 
• **Charanam:** The concluding section that provides variations and deeper explorations of the raga.
 
 
 
• **Role of Swaras in Varnam**
 
 
• Swara patterns in Varnam are used for strengthening control over rhythm and melody__.
 
• Muktayi Swaras and Charana Swaras are key segments that demonstrate the raga's nuances.
 
 
 
• **Carnatic Music Structure**
 __
 
• Carnatic music is deeply rooted in ragas__ (melodic frameworks) and __talas__ (rhythmic cycles).
 
• Compositions like Varnams, Kritis, and Tillanas serve as the foundation for its performance repertoire.

questions.question: The Mauryan period saw the development of which script for inscriptions?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Brahmi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Brahmi script** was the primary script used for inscriptions during the Mauryan period, particularly in Emperor Ashoka's edicts.
 
• It is one of the oldest writing systems in South Asia and is considered the **ancestor of most modern Indian scripts**, including Devanagari, Tamil, and Bengali.
 
• Brahmi was written from **left to right**, unlike Kharosthi, which was written from right to left.
 
• The inscriptions in Brahmi during the Mauryan period were often used to disseminate **Ashoka’s messages of Dhamma (moral and ethical principles)**.
 
• Deciphered by **James Prinsep in 1837**, the Brahmi script unlocked critical insights into ancient Indian history and culture.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kharosthi Script**

 
 
• This was another ancient script used in the northwestern parts of the Indian subcontinent, written from right to left.
 
• It was influenced by the Aramaic script and primarily used in the Gandhara region (modern-day Pakistan and Afghanistan).
 
 
 
• **Ashokan Edicts**
 
 
• The Mauryan Emperor Ashoka issued a series of inscriptions on rocks and pillars to propagate his policy of Dhamma.
 
• These edicts were written in Brahmi, Kharosthi, and other regional scripts depending on the location of the inscriptions.
 
 
 
• **Grantha Script**
 
 
• Grantha script was used in South India, primarily for writing Sanskrit texts.
 
• It developed much later and is not associated with the Mauryan period.
 
 
 
• **Pali and Prakrit**
 
 
• Pali and Prakrit are ancient languages, not scripts, often used in Buddhist and Jain texts.
 
• Many of Ashoka's inscriptions were written in Prakrit, but they used the Brahmi script.
 
 
 
• **James Prinsep’s Contribution**
 
 
• James Prinsep was a British scholar who deciphered the Brahmi and Kharosthi scripts in 1837.
 
• His work enabled historians to understand the Mauryan inscriptions and reconstruct India's ancient history.

questions.question: In the context of computer hardware components, what is the primary function of ROM?

options.text: It holds essential firmware required for booting the system
It physically supports all internal hardware modules
It stores temporary data used during system processing
It executes programs and handles arithmetic operations.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 1,

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• ROM (Read-Only Memory) is a type of non-volatile memory that retains its contents even when the computer is powered off.
 
• The primary function of ROM is to store essential firmware, such as the BIOS, which is required for booting the system.
 
• Firmware stored in ROM is hardcoded during manufacturing and is not meant to be modified by regular users.
 
• Unlike RAM, ROM does not lose its data when the system is shut down, making it critical for initializing hardware components during startup.
 
• ROM is used in various devices, including computers, smartphones, embedded systems, and gaming consoles, to provide stable and reliable operation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **BIOS (Basic Input/Output System)**

 
 
• The BIOS is firmware stored in ROM and is responsible for initializing hardware during the boot process.
 
• It provides an interface for the operating system to interact with the hardware components.
 
• Modern systems may use UEFI (Unified Extensible Firmware Interface) instead of traditional BIOS.
 
 
 
• **Non-Volatile Memory**
 
 
• Non-volatile memory retains data even when the power supply is cut off.
 
• Examples include ROM, EEPROM, and Flash memory.
 
• It is essential for storing permanent data or firmware.
 
 
 
• **EEPROM (Electrically Erasable Programmable Read-Only Memory)**
 
 
• EEPROM is a type of ROM that can be erased and reprogrammed electrically.
 
• It allows limited updates to firmware or settings stored on the device.
 
 
 
• **RAM vs ROM**
 
 
• RAM (Random Access Memory) is volatile and used for temporary data storage during system processing.
 
• ROM is non-volatile and stores permanent data, such as firmware.
 
• Both are essential for system operation but serve different purposes.

questions.question: When was the designation of the Governor General in India promoted as a Viceroy or Crown's representative?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Year 1858**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The title of **Governor-General of India** was replaced by the title of **Viceroy of India in 1858**, following the Government of India Act 1858.
 
• This change marked the formal transfer of authority from the **East India Company to the British Crown**, after the events of the Revolt of 1857 (also called the First War of Independence).
 
• The Viceroy acted as the **direct representative of the British Crown** and was responsible for administering India on behalf of the monarch.
 
• Lord Canning, who was the last Governor-General of India, became the **first Viceroy of India** in 1858.
 
• The **Government of India Act 1858** was a significant legislative change that centralized governance under the Crown, ending the dual control system of the East India Company.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Revolt of 1857:**

 
 
• Also known as India's First War of Independence, it was a major uprising against the rule of the British East India Company.
 
• The revolt led to significant political changes, including the abolition of the East India Company's rule in India.
 
 
 
• **Government of India Act 1858:**
 
 
• This act abolished the East India Company's authority and transferred governance directly to the British Crown.
 
• A new office called the "Secretary of State for India" was created to oversee Indian administration from Britain.
 
 
 
• **Role of the Viceroy:**
 
 
• The Viceroy served as the head of the colonial administration in India.
 
• He was responsible for implementing policies and laws on behalf of the British Crown.
 
 
 
• **Lord Canning:**
 
 
• He was the last Governor-General of India under the East India Company.
 
• He became the first Viceroy of India after the Government of India Act 1858 came into effect.
 
 
 
• **Significance of 1858:**
 
 
• The transition symbolized the beginning of the British Crown’s direct rule over India, which lasted until Indian independence in 1947.

questions.question: Which of the following rivers originates in the Western Ghats?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Krishna**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Krishna River originates in the **Western Ghats** near Mahabaleshwar in the state of Maharashtra, India.
 
• It is one of the longest rivers in India, with a total length of approximately **1,400 km**, flowing through Maharashtra, Karnataka, Telangana, and Andhra Pradesh.
 
• The river flows eastward and empties into the Bay of Bengal, supporting agriculture and irrigation along its course.
 
• Key tributaries of the Krishna River include the **Tungabhadra, Koyna, and Bhima Rivers**, among others.
 
• The Krishna River basin is known for its fertile lands and is a vital water source for millions in South India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Western Ghats**

 
 
• The Western Ghats are a mountain range that runs parallel to the western coast of India, known for their biodiversity and ecological significance.
 
• They are a UNESCO World Heritage Site and a major source of many important rivers in peninsular India.
 
 
 
• **Major Rivers Originating in the Western Ghats:**
 
 
• Besides Krishna, other important rivers originating from the Western Ghats include the Godavari, Kaveri, and Periyar.
 
• These rivers are crucial for irrigation, drinking water, and hydroelectric power generation in the southern states of India.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Krishna River:**
 
 
• The Krishna River is essential for agriculture, providing irrigation to large areas in the Deccan Plateau.
 
• It supports several major dams and irrigation projects, such as the Nagarjuna Sagar Dam and the Srisailam Dam.
 
 
 
• **Ecological Concerns:**
 
 
• Like many rivers in India, the Krishna River faces challenges such as pollution, over-extraction of water, and reduced flow due to climate change.
 
• Efforts are being made to conserve and sustainably manage the river and its basin.
